resolved_conflicts.explanation: Treated as one tower: the NHLR calls it Model Tower, Forest Lookouts calls a Stewart County Division of Forestry tower Barrow Hollow, and tnlandforms lists a Stewart County tower named Barrow. No source says these are the same tower outright; the story hedges on this.
The Register gives 611 ft (186 m) and tnlandforms gives 650 ft for the Barrow tower. No source explains the gap. The record keeps the Register figure.

The tower was built for the Tennessee Division of Forestry. The Register now lists the U.S. Forest Service as administrator, which fits the site being inside Land Between the Lakes, a USFS-administered recreation area.

notes_for_editor: Build and registration facts rest on the NHLR detail page, cross-checked against the Forest Lookouts and tnlandforms listings. No source dated after 2009 describes the tower itself; tnlandforms marks it standing with no date. The fire-detection line is the Register's description, now dated to its registration entry (November 3, 2009, its own evidence quote) rather than to a visit. The one web search found no Model Tower at Land Between the Lakes; its Bald Knob hits are a different tower and were not used. Access, staffing and fire history are unknown from these sources, so they are left out of facts and the story. No photos added; the NHLR photo is already in the record.
